evidence: The substrate for ellipsometry, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) measurements was a Czochralski grown n-type Si(100) wafer with a resistivity of 1–5U cm and a native silicon oxide layer which is approximately 2 nm thick. Films were also deposited on glass to study the band gap using ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis). The substrates were cleaned via 5 minute sonication steps each in acetone and ethanol with deionized water rinses between each solvent bath. Residual organics were then removed with a piranha clean (70% sulfuric acid and 30% hydrogen peroxide) for 15 minutes followed by a deionized water rinse and drying with pressurized air.
